description: Source inspection, mechanic decomposition, remix-aware blueprinting, and progression planning skills extracted from the clone inference stage.

skills.title: Describe the game as implemented
skills.intent: Map the actual current game before inventing the target remix direction.
required_actions: Identify genre, objective, fail state, score/progress state, input model, loop, and likely screen states.
Document current identity separately from intended remixed trajectory.
Ground all later analysis in observed code and behavior.
acceptance_bar: Current-game reality is clearly separated from remix ambition.
Later phases can use this mapping without guessing the original loop.
failure_modes_prevented: Fantasy detached from source reality
Misreading the actual loop
Remix stages preserving the wrong thing

skills.title: Decompose mechanics into protected and themable modules
skills.intent: Break the game into concrete mechanic surfaces and classify the risk level of each one.
required_actions: Decompose input, movement, timing, collision, scoring, hazard, reward, level/state, HUD, and feedback modules.
Classify each module as protected, themable, repairable, or unknown.
Record which surfaces may safely change versus which must remain intact.
acceptance_bar: Themable surfaces are concrete enough to guide world and visual phases.
failure_modes_prevented: Unsafe mechanic edits
Vague preserve/change guidance
Accidentally theming logic instead of presentation

skills.title: Assess true complexity and safe escalation knobs
skills.intent: Determine what kind of game this actually is and how complexity can increase without breaking it.
required_actions: Classify the game honestly: simple arcade, multi-state puzzle/action, physics-heavy, timing-heavy, and so on.
Identify complexity that may come from goals, readability, staged difficulty tuning, world evolution, and HUD clarity instead of risky rewrites.
Avoid fake complexity through unrelated mechanic invention.
acceptance_bar: Difficulty and complexity planning stay grounded in real game affordances.
Escalation logic remains compatible with protected mechanics.
failure_modes_prevented: Difficulty by random clutter
Unsafe rewrites disguised as escalation
Overstating what the game supports

skills.title: Turn the remix prompt into a coherent target game brief
skills.intent: Translate the user prompt into a recognizable, mechanically compatible future-facing remix premise.
required_actions: Write a remix premise that is generative, recognizable, and mechanically compatible.
Produce `Identity.json`, `RecreationPrompt.md`, and target-facing semantic tags.
Record preserve elements, transform elements, and confidence notes.
acceptance_bar: A downstream generator could recreate the intended remixed game from the analysis package.
Target identity is coherent and still grounded in source truth.
failure_modes_prevented: Weak remix premise
Disconnected target identity
Later stages guessing what the game should become

skills.title: Produce mechanics ranking, classification, and semantic tags
skills.intent: Preserve the inference-stage requirement to describe the intended remixed game in structured taxonomy outputs, not just prose.
required_actions: Rank the top gameplay-mechanics matches for the intended remixed game rather than the raw source game alone.
Write a companion classification artifact with scores, reasoning, inheritance notes, and uncertainty.
Generate semantic tags spanning theme, setting, characters, mechanics, mood, similar games, and preserve/transform identity.
acceptance_bar: The remixed game is described in both human-readable and machine-readable forms.
Later systems can classify or search the result without reverse-engineering prose.
failure_modes_prevented: Losing taxonomy outputs during prompt simplification
Only having a narrative description with no structured tags
Ranking mechanics for the wrong game target

skills.title: Define the 1.5-level core and five-level progression
skills.intent: Force explicit progression planning even when the source game lacks explicit levels.
required_actions: Define the smallest practical progression proof: Level 1 and Level 1.5.
Plan five levels of difficulty intent and five levels of visual evolution.
Specify safe knobs, protected mechanics, hazard/reward interpretation, HUD messaging, and visual beats for each level.
acceptance_bar: Progression semantics are defined even if explicit level files never exist.
World and visual phases can execute progression without guessing.
failure_modes_prevented: Flat remixes with no escalation logic
Late-stage guessing about level progression
Visual evolution detached from difficulty planning

skills.title: Preserve the embedded progressive-disclosure planning value
skills.intent: Carry forward the high-value level-adapter reasoning embedded in the inference stage without forcing separate level-file generation by default.
use_when: Whenever the remix needs explicit progression reasoning, even if it does not emit separate level HTML files.
required_actions: Explain what the player is learning, what is withheld, and what pressure is added across the intended progression curve.
Separate real difficulty dimensions from fake difficulty and clutter.
Document why the escalation model fits this specific game.
acceptance_bar: Progression is explainable as a learning and pressure curve rather than arbitrary tuning.
World and visual evolution can hang on a reasoned escalation model.
failure_modes_prevented: Losing the Nintendo-style progressive-disclosure value from the embedded source library
Escalation that is only numeric or decorative
No rationale for why progression fits the game

skills.title: Plan the procedural art system and downstream contract
skills.intent: Give later phases a reusable visual language plus explicit obligations.
required_actions: Define motif vocabulary, silhouettes, icon style, background layers, animation principles, and implementation preferences.
Write a downstream contract for world, visual, and QA execution.
Prefer structured `remix_plan_v4.json`-style outputs when feasible.
acceptance_bar: Later phases know what to preserve, draw, refine, and verify.
The procedural identity is specific enough to drive visuals and QA.
failure_modes_prevented: Visual style invented too late
No explicit phase handoff
Procedural art reduced to generic gradients
